diagnostic_evidence.quote: We derive wavenumber independent trace and Friedrichs-type

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract stresses general spatial dimension, and contribution b) presents the Friedrichs-type and trace estimates as valid for all wavenumbers with no dimensional restriction. Theorem thm:C_Friedrich and Corollary CorTrace are proved only for n>=3. The restriction is essential: for n=2, z_{0,0}(0)=0, so v=1 satisfies the DtN(0) condition with zero gradient and zero normal derivative, and the inequality fails.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the restriction n>=3 in the abstract and in contribution b), and note that the 2D Laplace limit fails.
issues.overall_effect: Readers are misled about the scope: the wavenumber-uniform Friedrichs and trace estimates are unavailable in two dimensions.
issues.title: Friedrichs/trace estimates advertised without the essential restriction n>=3
issues.why_classification: The formal results are correctly restricted; only the prose needs a scope qualification, and no mathematics changes.

issues.failure_explanation: Part 1b rests on (GreenStrong), which is deduced from the large-argument asymptotics (fundsysasy) applied to each term of the infinite series (uhutfourier). The O(z^{-1}) constants grow with mu (like a_1(mu) ~ mu^2/2). For any fixed r, the terms with mu much larger than |s|r are outside the asymptotic regime, so termwise bounds give no uniform bound on |u(r xi)| or on the radiation residual. A separate control of the tail is needed and is not supplied.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove the uniform decay through Green's representation u=DL(s)g-SL(s)psi together with the uniform asymptotics of the fundamental solution for y in S_R, or prove uniform-in-mu bounds on K_mu(sr)/K_mu(sR) to control the tail of the series.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that S_D(s)g satisfies IC^strong, and hence well-posedness under IC^strong for s≠0, is unsupported as proved.
issues.title: IC^Green => IC^strong derived from termwise asymptotics that are not uniform in m
issues.why_classification: A contained but nontrivial replacement argument is required; the statement itself survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This proof considers the unit disc $S_{1}$ ($R=1$) and the general case $R>0$

issues.failure_explanation: The proof is carried out for R=1. By scaling, -Re<DtN(s)g,g>_{S_R} >= ((n-2)/(2R))||g||^2_{L^2(S_R)}, not (n-2)/2. Counterexample: n=3, s=0, g constant gives z_{0,1/2}(0)=-1, so -Re<DtN(0)g,g> = ||g||^2/R, which is below ||g||^2/2 for R>2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace (n-2)/2 by (n-2)/(2R), which follows from the scaling already used in the proof.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit, supposedly sharp lower bound in (iii) is false for R>2. Its qualitative use (positivity for n>=3) survives.
issues.title: Lower bound in Theorem DtN (iii) lacks the 1/R scaling and is false for large R
issues.why_classification: A local constant correction suffices and no dependent argument changes.

issues.failure_explanation: For n=2 and m=0, Theorem thm:zmn only gives |Im z_{0,0}(s)| <= c_2+|Im s|. Indeed Im z_{0,0}(-ik) = 2/(pi M_0^2(k)) ~ pi/(2 log^2 k) as k->0, which is not O(k). So the displayed bound C(n)|Im s| ||g||^2 fails for constant g and small Im s. The proof of (iv) therefore rests on a false inequality.

(The completeness of $H$ follows from the continuity of the

issues.failure_explanation:
H is a union over z in C_{>=0} of solution sets.
- It is not a vector space, since sums of elements with different z need not satisfy any DtN condition.
- Its 'completeness' does not follow from continuity of DtN in z: the z_k may be unbounded, so the weak limit u need not satisfy a DtN condition for any s.
- The contradiction hypothesis uses the L^2(S_R) norm of the normal derivative instead of the H^{-1/2} norm in the statement, so a weaker inequality is addressed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair:
Argue along the sequence instead of passing to a limit in H:
- From ||d_r v_k||_{H^{-1/2}} -> 0 and boundedness in H^{1/2}, get <DtN(z_k)v_k,v_k> -> 0.
- The z-uniform lower bound ((n-2)/(2R))||v_k||^2_{L^2(S_R)} in Theorem thm:DtN (iii) then gives ||v_k||_{L^2(S_R)} -> 0.
- Compactness of the trace yields u|_{S_R}=0 for the constant limit u, a contradiction.
issues.overall_effect: The s-uniform Friedrichs inequality, and hence Corollary CorTrace, is not established by the given argument.
issues.title: Friedrichs proof uses a non-linear, non-closed set H as a Hilbert space
issues.why_classification: A short replacement argument is needed; the statement and constant independence survive.
